title: r-two56 food cogs SIBE replicates on fresh seeds 6 and 7: a local food cut kills the most isolated cog by t=655 on both, while its fed twin and every other body stay at 1.00; shell A1 0.96 at r=7, 0 in the core ring and outside
summary: Re-ran the claimed world (world.py, unchanged) on fresh seeds 6 and 7: labkit packs (192^2, t=1000; 12 and 19 final cogs, 0 splits, max 0.6-0.7 body lengths), then the claim's fork with its own scripts: runsave to t=600, mkcut picks the most isolated cog (nearest other core 57 px on seed 6, 35 px on seed 7) with a food-sink disk of r=18, then 300 t fed versus cut from the same checkpoint. On both seeds the cut cog drops below 10% of its matter at t=655 and is gone by t=900, while the same cog in the fed twin ends at 0.999-1.000 and all other bodies end at 0.999-1.000 in both arms (localcut.png, localcut.json). Cogs form from full-domain noise by t~85-135 (pack/seed6/sheet.png). The shell profile around isolated cogs on seed 6 (radial_cog.py, 64 cell-frames, t>=200): A1 1.00 at the centre, 0.00 at r=3 (the A0 ring), 0.96 at r=7, 0.00 at r=25-29.

by_construction: E (matter is built only from food and decays)
verdicts.limitation: I did not repeat the k4 shell-source ablation, so B rests on the profile plus the author's ablation. The cut is a permanent food sink, not just a stop to regrowth. Death is a collapse after a ~10% deficit, so the cog has little reserve. Cogs neither move nor divide, and food is plentiful, so there is no competition for it. The shell band is 4-5 px at R=10 with no resolution test.
